messages:
alex: Quick check — noticed a user saw model fallback even though route flag was OFF. Anyone else? I thought precedence is route > project > org > model. Repro below.

alex: Config snippet:
```
flag: enable_new_routing
scopes:
  org: false
  project: false
  route: false
  model: true
```

alex: Expected: off for route. Observed: requests to model X still went to new routing for a few minutes. Logs show fallback to model variant. Any ideas? @priya @sam

priya: Hmm. Did you check rollout audiences? If model has canary audience that matches trace id it may override? But our precedence shouldn't allow model to win.

sam: Can confirm I've seen similar once — caused by cached policy on router (prefix cache). If route-level change didn't invalidate prefix cache, runtime used old decision. Look for KV cache key TTLs.

alex: Good call — I see cache invalidation events were delayed for ~3m in region us-east-1. Is that expected on config push?

lee: There's a subtlety: route-level flag commit uses two-phase push: control-plane updates then router agent picks up. If agent restarts or misses heartbeat, it may fall back to local persisted model-level rule. We should add an explicit invalidation when route-level toggles.

config-bot: deploy-note: pushed flag change 1745067800 by alex — rollout=instant; agents notified.

sam: Actionable: add a short TTL (30s) on prefix decisions and emit metric when we apply route override. I can open a PR.

alex: That works. Also want a doc blurb in flags.md explaining expected eventual consistency and cache semantics.

priya: I'll add a one-paragraph note and link to ops playbook for rollback.

alex: Thanks. Sam — can you ping when PR lands? I'll validate on canary.

sam: Will do. ETA EOD. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout finished to canary 1745067900 — 2 hosts. no errors.

alex: Verified canary now honors route=false. Marking this resolved for now; follow-up PR for TTL + doc. Thanks team. :party:
